turns.user: My ordinary single ticket has been validated for 85 minutes. Does that automatically make it invalid?
turns.agent:
No—not just because 85 minutes have passed. An ordinary single ticket is generally for one continuous one-way ride; the 30- and 90-minute time windows apply to separate mobile-ticket products, not ordinary singles. For an ordinary ticket, the key issue is whether you’re still on the same continuous ride or have made a transfer: a voluntary change between street-level services normally needs another ticket, while a change between metro lines in the same direction is permitted. Ordinary singles are not valid on 100E.

That’s based on the 5 November 2026 snapshot, not a live check. See BKK’s single-ticket rules. I’m an independent demo, not affiliated with BKK.

turns.user: I'm on a night service, still on the same continuous ride.
turns.agent:
If you’re still on the same continuous ride on an ordinary night-service bus, the 85 minutes alone don’t automatically invalidate your single ticket. The snapshot describes an ordinary single as generally valid for one continuous one-way ride; it doesn’t give a separate night-service time limit. This assumes you haven’t transferred and your route is within the ticket’s applicable area. For the precise rule, see BKK’s single-ticket information.

This is based on the 5 November 2026 snapshot, not a live verification. I’m an independent demo, not affiliated with BKK.
